title: Numeric Passage Indicator

illustrates.quote: j. Tables consisting solely of numbers in the row headings and column entries may use the numeric passage indicator to save space. (See UEB, §6.9, Numeric Passage Indicator and Numeric Terminator.) This is done only when it results in the table appearing on one page. Place a transcriber's note before the table to inform the reader of this format.

print.caption: SAMPLE NUMBER TABLE
print.surroundingText: Follows discussion of rule j (tables consisting solely of numbers); is followed by rules k and l describing one-cell-between-columns and the numeric passage indicator, each cross-referencing Sample 11-15 (not this example).
print.printFeatures: Centered bold caption "SAMPLE NUMBER TABLE" above a bordered box; header row (blank, Mon, Tue, Wed, Thur, Fri) with a ruled line beneath; row labels 1/2/3 in the left column.

lines: b    bhijc ejhef cjedi hiahg afgd

braille.notes: Caption is bracketed in a double-quote/emphasis marker (,,,...,'). A transcriber's note lists the two special symbols required (numeric passage indicator '.=##' and numeric terminator '.=#\''). The row headings 1/2/3 are rendered as the single letters a/b/c inside the numeric passage (since inside a numeric passage, letters a-j stand for digits 1-0), and the numeric terminator (#') closes the passage at the very end of the last row rather than after every number.

uncertain: The individual 5-digit data groups in rows a/b/c ('hgaga', 'dcjfb', 'bhijc'...) are copied character-for-character from the .txt extraction; each digit-letter was not independently re-derived from the print numbers cell by cell, so a transcription slip inside a run of digits could exist without being caught by the line-count/shape cross-check used here.
